props.prompt: A home-made reactive steel shooting target on a stand seen straight from the front: at the top an octagonal steel plate painted with chipped white and faded red rings and pocked with bullet dents, bolted through a thick coil spring onto a rusty tripod welded from rebar, a tan sandbag draped over the tripod feet to weigh it down, a small cream paper pawn tag tied to the frame with string, proportions about two wide to five tall.

A battered rubber sparring dummy seen straight from the side: an armless humanoid torso and bald head moulded from dark red-brown rubber, mounted on a thick steel coil spring on a round weighted base made from an old truck wheel rim, grey duct-tape patches on the ribs, old slash marks, a white chalk cross drawn on the chest, a small cream paper pawn tag tied round the neck, proportions about two wide to five tall.

The armless body of a home-built sparring machine seen straight from the front: a squat steel column welded from a salvaged washing-machine drum and car engine parts on a heavy bolted base plate with two sandbags on it, a round steel hub at shoulder height with one empty axle socket on its left side and one on its right side, a wire-caged signal lamp with dark unlit glass on the very top, exposed black cables, a yellow and black hazard striped band around the waist, a small cream paper pawn tag, the machine has no arms at all, proportions about two wide to five tall.

One single mechanical striker arm lying perfectly horizontal seen straight from the side: a grey steel tube with a bolted pivot ring at the left end and a fat red-brown leather boxing pad wrapped with grey tape at the right end, a short hydraulic damper along the tube, proportions about five wide to one tall.

A photo-sensor timing gate post seen straight from the side: a slim grey steel pole on a small weighted tripod base, yellow and black hazard tape wound around the pole, a boxy sensor head on top with a round dark glass lens facing right and a small unlit signal lamp above it, a coiled black cable running down the pole, a small cream paper pawn tag, proportions about one wide to six tall.
